newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition gets thumbs down in Herald poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition gets thumbs down in Herald poll.

text.p: The National-New Zealand First Coalition Government has been rejected out of hand in a nationwide survey of voters taken after 100 days in office, the New Zealand Herald said on Friday.
Nearly seven out of 10 of the 700 people polled in the past week said they were not satisfied with the performance of the government so far "and they seem to blame NZ First," the paper said.

Support for NZ first and its leader, Winston Peters, nosedived in the poll, taken by the research unit at Waikato University. Natonal's support has risen, as has Labour's since the October election and the last survey in December.
In the preferred prime minister stakes, Peters has sunk to just 3.1 percent, his lowest level since he began his rise in that category nearly nine years ago.
Bolger was the preferred prime minister with 31 percent, and Labour's Helen Clark was second with 21 percent.
The Alliance's Jim Anderton had 7.6 percent support and Labour's Mike Moore had 6.5 percent.
The Herald said 68.3 percent of those polled said they were not satisfied with the coalition, 19.8 percent said they were and 11.9 percent were unsure.
